Title: SQL Injection in customer export endpoint
OWASP Description: Untrusted data is interpreted as part of a command or query (SQL, NoSQL, OS command, LDAP, expression language) and executed with unintended privileges.

Title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) on invoice endpoint
OWASP Description: Restrictions are not correctly enforced, enabling users to act outside their intended permissions, access unauthorized functions or data, escalate privileges, or perform forced browsing and IDOR.

Title: SSRF via PDF generator allows internal network scanning
OWASP Description: Server-side application fetches a remote resource supplied by the attacker without validation, allowing access to internal services, cloud metadata and internal networks.

Title: Weak TLS cipher suites on corporate VPN
OWASP Description: Failures related to cryptography — missing or weak encryption, insecure key management, cleartext transmission or storage of sensitive data and non-compliant use of algorithms.

Title: Privileged access via default admin token in developer console
OWASP Description: Restrictions are not correctly enforced, enabling users to act outside their intended permissions, access unauthorized functions or data, escalate privileges, or perform forced browsing and IDOR.

Title: Outdated third-party library with known RCE (Apache Log4j core)
OWASP Description: Use of components (libraries, runtimes, packages, sub-systems) with known vulnerabilities, end-of-life software, or components not patched to a supported state.

Title: Security events not logged for failed administrative logins
OWASP Description: Insufficient logging, detection, monitoring and active response, enabling attacks to go unnoticed and preventing post-incident forensics.

Title: Unused services exposed on public firewall rules
OWASP Description: Insecure defaults, open cloud storage, unnecessary features, default accounts, verbose errors and incomplete hardening of the technology stack.
NIST Controls: CM-6, CM-7, CM-8, CM-11, SC-7, SI-2

Title: Missing rate limiting on password reset allows MFA bypass
OWASP Description: Broken authentication, weak password policy, credential stuffing, session fixation, missing MFA and insecure session management.
NIST Controls: IA-2, IA-5, IA-8, IA-11, AC-7, AC-8
